content_preview.title: Ryan Dahl Releases Celld, a Self-Hosted Open-Source Alternative to Cloudflare's Durable Objects
content_preview.summary: Node.js and Deno creator Ryan Dahl has open-sourced celld, letting developers run Cloudflare's Durable Objects and Workers APIs on their own S3-backed infrastructure.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Ryan Dahl, the creator of Node.js and Deno, has released celld, an open-source daemon that lets developers run Cloudflare's Workers and Durable Objects JavaScript APIs on their own infrastructure instead of Cloudflare's, according to [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/08/12/nodejs-creator-liberates-durable-objects-from-cloudflare-with-celld/5286954). Dahl's project is compatible with Cloudflare's Workers and Durable Objects APIs but claims it costs significantly ...

editor_notes.content_quality: Long, technically dense News piece that handles a dueling-figures dispute (Dahl's cost estimate vs. Cloudflare's rebuttal) correctly by attributing each number to its source rather than picking a winner. Correctly verifies the internal cross-link to the March 2026 Deno 2.7 article before use.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both snapshots directly. The Register confirms every quote and figure attributed to it verbatim: the 'orders of magnitude cheaper at scale' quote, the $415/$49/$20.65 cost figures (Cloudflare's rebuttal figure appears in the source as 'cost only $20.65 to house on Cloudflare' rather than '...a month', but the meaning and monthly-cost context match), the Kenton Varda attribution and 'one of the best primitives' quote, the AWS Lambda comparison, the 2020 launch date, WebSocket/Hibernate mode description, the AI Gateway/serverless SQL usage, the Apache 2 license, the Rust/C/C++/Go/Zig-via-WebAssembly claim, the Hacker News quote, and the Neon Functions mention. One trivial, meaning-preserving discrepancy: the article quotes The Register's 'the world's fastest web applications' with a lowercase 'w', while the source has 'Web' capitalized -- a capitalization-only difference with zero semantic impact, not worth a corrections note. celld's own GitHub README confirms every technical quote verbatim: the self-description, the no-control-plane/no-consensus bucket coordination, the 'applications shard by construction' and 'inactive cell costs nearly nothing' quotes, the compare-and-swap ownership mechanism, the 'durable source of truth' quote, the Linux x86-64/ARM64 container images and shell-script installer, and both quoted lines about pull requests being disabled.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics trace verbatim to their cited sources. No hallucinations or misattributions found.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral; presents Dahl's cost claims and Cloudflare's rebuttal side by side without endorsing either.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate -- no prior archive coverage of celld.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Approve. Every quote and figure verified against both sources (one trivial, non-substantive capitalization difference noted but not correction-worthy); the internal cross-link was verified to resolve. No corrections needed.
